workload: Fully-async multi-turn agentic RL on a 16A3B-class MoE model (Miles + SGLang + Megatron), 16 GPUs split 8 train / 8 rollout across two pods (master + worker). Each trajectory is a multi-turn tool-using episode in a remote sandbox; conversation history grows to >10k tokens, so per-turn latency depends on whether the previous turn's KV prefix is still cached on the engine that serves the next turn.
question: With routing fixed, why are the rollout engines still starved, and what restores throughput?

run-a.description: Routing fixed: miles router and session gateway disabled, sglang router with cache_aware policy. Sandbox gate unchanged.
run-a.log_coverage: pod-console tail only (last 2000 master lines, ~17:17-17:41) + 270 worker lines; the in-process console capture for this run is empty

run-b.description: Routing fixed and sandbox admission gate opened.
run-b.log_coverage: in-process console capture (17:55-18:41) + pod-console tail to job end (~18:53)

notes: In-flight trajectories = max_inflight_groups x samples_per_group (32 x 8 = 256 for the post-migration runs). The sandbox setup gate is an asyncio semaphore held for sandbox create + setup + up to 3 retries; every trajectory must pass it before its first turn.
Semaphore waits are only logged when the wait exceeds 5 s ('sandbox setup waited Xs for semaphore').
